import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Determinantal conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinantal_conjecture)
-/

/- Formalisation note: Here, we represent the two normal matrices as $U_1 D_1 U_1^*$ and
$U_2 D_2 U_2^*$ respectively, where $U_1, U_2$ are unitary and $D_1, D_2$
are diagonal. This is an universal form of a normal matrix,
allowing to retrieve $\lambda (A)_i$ as ${D_1}_{i,i}$, whereas the current mathlib
doesn't support obtaining the vector of eigenvalues from a general normal
non-Hermitian matrix. -/

namespace DeterminantalConjecture

/--
Does the determinant of the sum $A + B$ of two $n \times n$ normal
complex matrices $A$ and $B$ always lie in the convex hull
of the $n!$ points $\prod\_i (\lambda(A)\_i + \lambda(B)\_{\sigma(i)})$?
Here the numbers $\lambda(A)\_i$ and $\lambda(B)\_i$ are
the eigenvalues of $A$ and $B$, and $\sigma$ is an element of the symmetric
group $S\_n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15]
theorem determinantal_conjecture
    (n : Type) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (d1 d2 : n → ℂ) (U1 U2 : unitary (Matrix n n ℂ)) :
    (U1 * Matrix.diagonal d1 * star U1 + U2 * Matrix.diagonal d2 * star U2).det
      ∈ convexHull ℝ { ∏ i, (d1 i + d2 (σ i)) | σ : Equiv.Perm n } := by
  sorry

end DeterminantalConjecture

reformulations.difference: Instead of quantifying over normal matrices and extracting their eigenvalues, Lean quantifies over arbitrary complex diagonal lists and independent unitary matrices, representing each matrix as U * diagonal d * star U.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The complex spectral theorem says precisely that every normal matrix has such a unitary diagonalization. Conversely, every matrix of this form is normal, and its characteristic polynomial is ∏ i, (X - C (d i)), so the diagonal list gives its eigenvalues with multiplicity. Thus these parameters cover exactly the matrix pairs in the source, without requiring simultaneous diagonalization. Reordering either eigenvalue list merely reindexes the permutations generating the hull. The real convex hull in ℂ is the source's ordinary geometric convex hull. Arbitrary finite index types amount to reindexing ordinary square matrices; the additional empty-index case is harmless because both the determinant and the sole permutation product are 1.

review.notes: The file's sole theorem faithfully states the cited conjecture. Supporting checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without invoking the conjecture: normality and the characteristic polynomial of UDU*, invariance under eigenvalue reordering, empty and one-dimensional cases, and diagonal and zero-list cases. A noncommuting rational 2×2 sample gives determinant 16/25 and permutation products 0 and 1. No status discrepancy was found in the cited article. The full spectral-theorem equivalence was checked mathematically, not proved in Lean. Primary-reference access was limited: de Oliveira's publisher returned HTTP 403, and Marcus's downloaded PDF was not successfully extracted; the faithfulness conclusion rests on the explicit Wikipedia statement and the spectral-theorem characterization.
